subject: No-train attestation and geo-snapshot request for MedaLabs pilot
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <ecruz@medalabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedaLabs Procurement <procurement@medalabs.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: No-train attestation + geo snapshot for pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move the pilot forward. As part of procurement and our privacy review, Legal has asked for two items before we can sign the pilot SOW:

1) A signed attestation confirming Redwood will not use MedaLabs pilot data to improve or train models (no-training / no-improve clause).
2) A brief operational "geo-snapshot" that lists the regions and subprocessors that will process the pilot traffic, plus KMS locations and confirmation on whether any subprocessors are outside the US/EU.

They want enough detail to show us who will touch the data and an evidence path (logs, residency map) rather than full internal docs. Could you share these items by next Wednesday (2028-03-22)?

I attached a template attestation Legal provided that shows the fields they expect (template_attestation.pdf). If you prefer to provide an operational snapshot + signed cover letter, that can work too.

Short timeline is important for us — procurement would like to close the pilot this sprint. Please let me know who on your side I should expect these from and any blockers.

Best,
Elena Cruz
Head of Data Governance
MedaLabs

Attachments: template_attestation.pdf

- David: can you confirm current subprocessor inventory for the hosted inference path (including any cloud partners, logging, metrics, S3 buckets) and attach a regional map for KMS keys? A CSV with role/region/status is perfect.

If any of this is a blocker we should let them know and propose the alternative (signed cover letter + operational evidence). I can be the primary contact to Elena.

Hannah

Subject: Re: Request: No-train attestation + geo snapshot for pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Per our internal review we can deliver the following by Tuesday 2028-03-21: 

- Signed attestation: we will sign your provided template attesting that Redwood will not use MedaLabs pilot data to train or improve our models, subject to the narrow operational exclusions noted below. Attached: redlined_attestation.pdf (our signed cover)
- Operational geo-snapshot bundle: subprocessor inventory CSV, KMS regional map, and a redacted log sample demonstrating that model improvement pipelines are not connected to pilot traffic. Attached: subprocessor_inventory_20280316.csv, kms_region_map.png
- DPA addendum: Lauren has prepared a narrow DPA addendum that mirrors the attestation and includes a short audit-rights clause and evidence-delivery SLA. Attached: redline_dpa_v1.docx

A couple of clarifying notes for procurement/legal:
- "No-train" commitment: Redwood will not use pilot interaction payloads to update weights or train models. This commitment excludes aggregated telemetry (e.g., anonymized system metrics used for capacity planning) and standard monitoring traces. If MedaLabs requires absolute exclusion of any telemetry, tell us and we'll scope that in the addendum.
- Subprocessors: the CSV lists vendors that process logs/metrics for operations; none have access to raw token content unless specifically provisioned in Dedicated setups. We'll flag any exceptions.

Next steps: please confirm if your Legal team will accept Redwood's signed attestation + operational bundle or whether they require an additional DocuSign execution flow. Once you confirm I will ask Lauren to finalize the addendum and David/Kimberly to push the final artifacts.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
